title: Miss Margaret and Kimball: Hot Springs and Shreveport theaters
summary: Love describes Kimball's wife the pianist, their job in Hot Springs and return to the Hippodrome in Shreveport, while Love worked at the Star.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Miss Margaret. Kimber's wife. They come back, you know. They went to Hot Spring. Lucius Wilson wanted me to come there to play, you see. And I knew Kimber was the man for him. So I told Kimber. And his wife was playing all the time in May and Neely. Before May and Neely. That's the way it was at the theater. And her and Kimber had taken this job and went to work for Lucius J. Wilson. I don't know for what reason. Well, he didn't work long. About two or three months. The job blew up or something. And he come back to Shreveport where I had been playing around there. At the Star Theater. I believe he went in there. They call it. Across the street. They call it. What the theater in there. Hippodrome. Called the Hippodrome Theater. Right across the street from the Star Theater. I used to work at the Star. In Shreveport? In Shreveport. In Shreveport. So Kimber and his wife went to work there. And I was working with John Rubishow in the place where he had just left, you see. I don't know what would come of him after that. He went on out in Hot Springs somewhere again. I think he died. He come back there before he died. I don't know whether his wife lived or not. She must be dead too. They were very old people, you know.
